scope: Native InnoDB child supporting-index replacement during pure addition or atomic foreign-key exchange.
profile: Native release, utf8mb4, exact absolute table names, empty sql_mode and referential checks enabled.
rules: A native ordinary full child index created for a foreign-key constraint has a generated-origin role. CREATE TABLE LIKE carries that role to the copied physical key.
Find which proposed native directional fields require an index after considering the original supported prefixes and the selected proposed prefixes.

An original generated key of exactly the proposed directional width cannot suppress the new generated candidate. Prefer the new candidate and replace the original. An original generated key with a strictly longer matching prefix can still support the new constraint. An explicit matching key can supply support at equal or greater width.
For each new index, replace any full earlier implicit child index when its complete ordered directional fields form a prefix of the new physical key. An explicit prior physical key remains present.
Remove superseded keys from the prior name space before allocating the successor names. Reuse of the physical name is possible. Previous foreign constraint labels remain independently occupied.
Enforce the native 64-key bound on the final native key set, including an explicit primary key. Statically invalid original catalogs are rejected where declarations are constructed.
The completed value carries the resolved physical names that disappear and the exact created key references. The constructor uses native index-origin facts and unaffected keys as transient inputs.
observations: Distinguish the same name with different physical column width. Record before and after full ordered directions, origin fixture and the name of each replacement.
Compare implicit originals, explicit controls, copied implicit origin, named and automatic successors, name reuse and the final physical budget with one through 64 existing keys.
Verify persistent rows, constraint matches, unaffected values and both native execution routes under the same exact reference and type meanings.

Distinguish equal-width replacement of the implicit physical name, retention of a longer original key, an explicit equal-width control, and orphaned implicit keys after removal of their original edge.
trust: Native table DDL declarations and copied physical metadata
The independent native observers and actual shape checks
faults: Forget origin or protect an implicit old key from replacement
